translationRepairs: Under Hui and Huai the heartland exploded into chaos; after the court crossed to the south, authority fractured among factions. Emperor Yuan likened his restoration to Shao Kang's revival, yet Wang Dun blocked him; the deposed emperor at Haixi echoed King Changyi's scandal on a lesser scale, and Huan Wen upset the proper order. Fear of raw coercion turned indulgence into habit.

Under Hui and Huai the heartland exploded into chaos; after the court crossed to the south, authority fractured among factions. Emperor Yuan likened his restoration to Shao Kang's revival, yet Wang Dun blocked him; the Prince of Haixi reproduced King Changyi's offenses on a lesser scale, and Huan Wen upset the proper order. Once coercion by the powerful became the worry, loose restraint hardened into custom.

海西微昌邑之罪 rates Haixi's own offenses as slighter than Changyi's; the original 'echoed...on a lesser scale' is close, but 'deposed emperor' is not in this unit. 羈縻成俗 is loose restraint becoming custom, not 'indulgence'. The proposal's wholesale rewrite of accurate first clauses is stylistic; courtesy-name mappings 處仲/元子 are already correctly given as Wang Dun and Huan Wen.

When the duke of Changdao succeeded, his title rose to marquis of Lai township with eight hundred more households; he supervised Qing military affairs as General Who Rouses Might and inspector of Qing, then shifted to General Who Pacifies the East.

When the duke of Changdao succeeded, his title rose to marquis of Lai township with eight hundred more households; he supervised Qing military affairs as General Who Displays Martial Might and inspector of Qing, then shifted to General Who Pacifies the East.
The office is 振武將軍; rendering it identically to 振威 as 'Rouses Might' erases the 武/威 distinction. 'Displays Martial Might' matches 振武.

When the Duke of Changdao Township ascended the throne, his noble rank was advanced to Marquis of Lai Township, another eight hundred households were added to his fief, he was promoted to supervise military affairs in Qing Province with concurrent appointment as General Who Rouses Might and Inspector of Qing Province, and transferred to General Who Pacifies the East.

When the Duke of Changdao Township ascended the throne, his noble rank was advanced to Marquis of Lai Township, another eight hundred households were added to his fief, he was promoted to supervise military affairs in Qing Province with concurrent appointment as General Who Displays Martial Might and Inspector of Qing Province, and transferred to General Who Pacifies the East.
Literal English likewise collapses 振武 into the same 'Rouses Might' used for 振威; the replacement correctly distinguishes 振武將軍.

Before Wei had set out, the commandant [duwei] under Zhi's tent asked leave and returned home, secretly supplied provisions over a hundred li down the road, intercepted Wei as a companion, and assisted him at every turn.

Before Wei had set out, the commander (dudu) under Zhi's tent asked leave and returned home, secretly supplied provisions over a hundred li down the road, intercepted Wei as a companion, and assisted him at every turn.
The office is 都督 (dudu), not 都尉; the gloss [duwei] is wrong. The proposal's (dudu) is the right reading, but keeping English 'commandant' still maps to 都尉; 'commander (dudu)' matches 帳下都督.
He rose to supervise Yu military affairs as General of the Right and inspector of Yu, entered the Masters of Writing, and picked up the additional title cavalry conductor.
He rose to supervise Yu military affairs as General of the Right and inspector of Yu, entered the Masters of Writing, and received the additional title Commandant of Imperial Equipages.
奉車都尉 is Commandant of Imperial Equipages; 'cavalry conductor' is a different office.
Hu Wei's younger brother Pi (courtesy Jixiang) was likewise capable, rising to inspector of Yi and General Who Pacifies the East.
Hu Wei's younger brother Pi (courtesy Jixiang) was likewise capable, rising to inspector of Yi and General Who Calms the East.
s0092 has 安東將軍, not 平東將軍 of the preceding sentence; 'Calms the East' preserves the 安/平 distinction.
After the Luoyang catastrophe he fled south; Wang Dun nominated him for Yi Province so he could join Yidu prefect Liu Chun in defending the Ba gorges.
After the Luoyang catastrophe he fled south; Wang Dun nominated him for Yi Province so he could join Yidu prefect Liu Chun in holding Baidi.
白帝 is the fortress Baidi; 'Ba gorges' invents a geographic gloss the Chinese does not use.
As filial-and-incorrupt nominee he became magistrate of Gaomen county.
As filial-and-incorrupt nominee he became magistrate of Haomen county.
浩亹 is Haomen; reading 浩 as Gao is a transcription error.
Usher Dou Yun, formerly magistrate of Gaomen, was praised west of the River for diligent cultivation and pure conduct.
Usher Dou Yun, formerly magistrate of Haomen, was praised west of the River for diligent cultivation and pure conduct.
The same county 浩亹 recurs in the edict; Haomen is required for consistency with the source.
Cao Shu (courtesy Yuanyuan) came from Qiao in the Qiao princedom.
Cao Shu (courtesy Yanyuan) came from Qiao in the Qiao princedom.
字顏遠 is Yanyuan; Yuanyuan misreads 顏 as 元.
Cao Shu, courtesy name Yuanyuan, was a native of Qiao in the Principality of Qiao.
Cao Shu, courtesy name Yanyuan, was a native of Qiao in the Principality of Qiao.
Literal field repeats the same misreading of 顏遠 as Yuanyuan.
His grandfather Cao Zhao had been Wei general who guards the borders.
His grandfather Cao Zhao had been Wei General of the Guards.
魏衛將軍 is the Wei-period General of the Guards, not a border-guard title.
His grandfather Zhao was General Who Guards Wei.
His grandfather Zhao was Wei General of the Guards.
Parsing 魏衛將軍 as 'General Who Guards Wei' treats 魏 as the object of 衛; 魏 marks the dynasty and 衛將軍 is the office.
Wuling prefect Dai Chang fancied himself a wit; Pan Jing played dumb until Dai sent him to spar with Dai Yuan—then he revealed his depth.

Administrator Dai Chang of Wuling also loved Pure Talk; when he sparred with Jing, Jing humored him; Chang thought himself superior, laughed him off, and sent him to debate his son Ruosi—only then did Jing unfurl his full argument.
The son is named only 若思; Dai Yuan is not in this unit. The original also omits 昌以為不如己 and Jing's initial 假借.
Section heading — Fan Gui (the Wikisource line wraps the surname with editorial markup).
The Chinese is only the heading 范晷; the Wikisource-markup gloss is not a translation.
His widowed sister had left a grandson, Mai; Fan Guang fled south with the boy on his back and never abandoned him to bandits.
His elder sister had married into the Sun clan and died early, leaving a grandson Mai; Guang carried him south in flight; though bandits pressed hard, he never abandoned the child.
適孫氏，早亡 states marriage into the Sun clan and early death, not widowhood; the proposed text matches the source.
Zhong Hui's western campaign spotted his talent and pulled him from Mengchi magistrate to chief clerk.
Zhong Hui's campaign against Shu spotted his talent and pulled him from Mengchi magistrate to chief clerk.
伐蜀 names the campaign against Shu; 'western campaign' drops that object.
In the first year of Xianhe, Posthumous honors included minister of the imperial household, gold seal, purple ribbon, and a pig offering.
In the first year of Xianhe he died; posthumous honors included minister of the imperial household, a gold seal and purple ribbon, and sacrifice with a young pig.
咸和元年卒 records his death before the posthumous honors; the original omits 卒.

When Kangbo became Minister of Personnel, Yin-zhi thereupon ascended to pure ranks; leaving common cloth he became clerk of merit for General Who Supports the State, transferred to join staff on the campaign against Rong.

When Kangbo became Minister of Personnel, Yin-zhi thereupon ascended to pure ranks; leaving common cloth he became clerk of merit for General Who Supports the State, then transferred as administrator on the staff of the General Who Campaigns Against the Caitiffs.
參征虜軍事 is appointment to the staff of the General Who Campaigns Against the Caitiffs, not a campaign against the Rong.
Central posts stacked up—secretariat, academy, heir's guard, historian, left guard.
Central posts stacked up—secretariat, academy, heir's guard, and historian.
This sentence ends at 領著作郎; 左衛將軍 belongs to s0393 and is invented here.

He entered [court] as vice director of the Secretariat, academician of the imperial academy, commander of the heir's right guard; transferred palace attendant and concurrently compiler; promoted General of the Left Guard.

He entered [court] as vice director of the Secretariat, academician of the imperial academy, and commander of the heir's right guard; transferred to cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, concurrently compiler.
轉散騎常侍，領著作郎 does not include 左衛將軍, which appears only in the following sentence; cavalier attendant-in-ordinary is the correct office.
In the ninth year he died; posthumously awarded vice minister of the imperial household with concurrent imperial household aide.
In the ninth year he died; posthumously awarded Left Minister of the Imperial Household, with cavalier attendant-in-ordinary added.
左光祿大夫 is Left Minister of the Imperial Household; 加散騎常侍 adds cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, not an imperial-household aide.

From Zi Chan in Zheng and Ximen Bao in Ye to Huang Ba in Yingchuan and Wen Weng in Shu—some overawed corrupt clerks, some won deep affection, some spread Confucian reform through Qi and Lu, some ruled with calm kindness—history praised them, and capable officials ever since have taken them as their yardstick.

From Zi Chan in Zheng and Ximen Bao in Ye to Huang Ba in Yingchuan and Wen Weng in Shu—some overawed corrupt clerks, some won deep affection, some made instruction equal that of Qi and Lu, some ruled with calm kindness—history praised them, and capable officials ever since have taken them as their yardstick.
教移齊魯 means instruction was brought up to the Qi-Lu standard, not that Confucian reform was spread through Qi and Lu; the replacement keeps the rest of the human sentence and corrects that geography.
At every hostel he watered his mount, gathered firewood, cooked his meal, ate, and moved on with other travelers.
At every hostel he personally tended the donkey, gathered firewood, cooked his meal, ate, and moved on with other travelers.
躬放驢 is personally turning out or tending the donkey; the original invents watering and a generic mount, while the preceding sentence already has him driving a donkey alone.

He was repeatedly promoted to supervise military affairs in Yu Province with concurrent appointment as General of the Right and Inspector of Yu Province, entered [court] as Masters of Writing, and was additionally given Cavalry Conductor.

He was repeatedly promoted to supervise military affairs in Yu Province with concurrent appointment as General of the Right and Inspector of Yu Province, entered [court] as Masters of Writing, and was additionally given Commandant of Imperial Equipages.
奉車都尉 is Commandant of Imperial Equipages; Cavalry Conductor would render a different cavalry office, and the idiomatic line already has the correct title.
He later governed eastern Xiang and served as palace gentleman to Prince Chengdu, then died in office of illness.
He later governed Xiangdong and served as Chamberlain of the Palace Gentlemen to Prince Chengdu, then died of illness.
湘東太守 is Administrator of Xiangdong, not 'eastern Xiang', and 郎中令 is Chamberlain of the Palace Gentlemen to Prince Chengdu; 病卒 states death by illness without 卒於官.
Recommended as filial and incorrupt, he was appointed magistrate of Gaomen.
Recommended as filial and incorrupt, he was appointed magistrate of Haomen.
浩亹 is Haomen; Gaomen misreads 浩, and the idiomatic line and office claims already use Haomen.
Usher Dou Yun, formerly magistrate of Gaomen, was praised west of the River for diligent cultivation and pure conduct.
Usher Dou Yun, formerly magistrate of Haomen, was praised west of the River for diligent cultivation and pure conduct.
The same toponym 浩亹 appears in the edict; the literal field must match Haomen, not Gaomen.
Promoted to Julu, he compiled a notable administrative record.
Promoted to Administrator of Julu, he compiled a notable administrative record.
遷钜鹿太守 names the commandery administratorship, a promotion from county magistrate; 'Promoted to Julu' drops 太守.
His elder sister had married into the Sun clan and died early, leaving a grandson Mai; Guang carried him south in flight; though bandits pressed hard, he never abandoned the child.
His elder sister had married into the Sun clan and died early, leaving a son named Mai; Guang carried him south in flight; though bandits pressed hard, he never abandoned the child.
After 姊適孫氏, 有孫名邁 is the Sun-surnamed son Mai left by the sister, whom Guang carried south; reading 孫 as 'grandson' adds a generation the Chinese does not support.
The court sent imperial household aide Huan Yi and Yu Wei to comfort the starving and observe whether things were well—then impeached You for unauthorized grain issue.
The court sent Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary Huan Yi and Yu to comfort the starving and observe whether things were well, then impeached You for unauthorized grain issue.
散騎常侍桓彝、虞慰勞饑人 sends Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary Huan Yi and a colleague surnamed Yu to comfort the starving; 慰勞 is the verb, not a given name Wei, and 散騎常侍 is not 'imperial household aide'.
He exceeded ritual mourning his mother.
Serving his mother he was filial and careful; when he observed mourning, his grief exceeded ritual.
事母孝謹 is living filial care of his mother, then 及其執喪，哀毀過禮 is later mourning that exceeded ritual; the original omits the first clause and collapses the sequence.
Lu Zhi stayed loyal to Wei; Sima Yi spared him—perhaps victors still needed moral examples.

Lu Zhi exhausted fidelity to the house of Cao, forcing gates and breaking barriers; Emperor Xuan stayed his thunderbolt wrath and rewarded that steadfast loyalty—once mastery was his, did he not still want men whose integrity even critics must acknowledge?

The original drops 犯門斬關 and reduces 收雷霆之威，獎忠貞之烈 to Sima Yi sparing him, but the proposal's 'martyrdom' is wrong: 烈 here is loyal ardor, and he was rewarded, not martyred. Keep the established personal name Lu Zhi while restoring 世英/曹氏, 宣帝, and the rhetorical close.
Seeing his integrity and learning he still owned no house, the emperor ordered fifty rooms built for him.
Seeing that Zhi was pure, loyal, and upright in conduct and had never owned a house, the emperor ordered fifty rooms built for him.
The original 'integrity and learning' misrenders 清忠履正, which praises purity, loyalty, and upright conduct, not scholarship; the replacement matches the Chinese and remains natural English.
Emperor Ming of Wei granted this; an edict was still issued praising him, encouraging him with the fine example of Huang Ba, and he was promoted to General Who Suppresses Brigands.
Emperor Ming of Wei granted this; an edict was still issued praising him, encouraging him with the fine example of Huang Ba, and he was additionally granted the title General Who Suppresses Brigands.
加討寇將軍 marks an additional concurrent title, so 'promoted' overstates a replacement; 'additionally granted the title' is accurate.
The court mourned him, enriched his grave goods, gave the posthumous name Zhen ('steadfast'), and allotted one hundred mu of burial land.
The emperor held mourning for him, burial gifts were given beyond the norm, his posthumous name was Zhen ('steadfast'), and he was granted a burial plot of one hundred mu.
帝為舉哀 makes the emperor the mourner; 'the court' wrongly shifts the agent, and the rest of the replacement follows 賵贈有加, 諡曰貞, 賜塋田百畝.
Wei once remonstrated that current policy was too lenient; the emperor said: 'Below the Masters of Writing supervisors, I grant no indulgence.'
Wei once remonstrated that current policy was too lenient; the emperor said: 'Below the gentlemen of the Masters of Writing, I grant no indulgence.'
尚書郎 is the gentlemen/lang of the Masters of Writing, not 'supervisors'; Hu Wei's next reply about 丞郎令史 confirms a grade line, not a supervisory office.
Later promoted Administrator of Xiangdong, he served as palace gentleman to Prince Chengdu Sima Ying; died of illness.
Later promoted Administrator of Xiangdong, he served as Chamberlain of the Palace Attendants (langzhongling) to Prince Chengdu Sima Ying; died of illness.
郎中令 is the princely chamberlain of palace attendants, not ordinary 郎中 'palace gentleman'; the replacement restores the correct office.
Under Wei he entered the central ministries, rose to gentleman of the Masters of Writing, and served as palace attendant.
Under Wei he was summoned to a ducal office, rose by steps to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, and served as Supervising Secretary.
辟公府 is a summons to a ducal office, not entry into the central ministries; 累遷尚書郎 and 曆給事中 are stepwise promotion then Supervising Secretary, which the original 'palace attendant' blurs with 侍中.
Soon he commanded the guards, ran Henan, and took the granaries ministry—but the humane magistrate was gone; he turned petty and cruel.
Soon he was promoted Commandant of the Guards, Intendant of Henan, and Minister of Agriculture, but he no longer had a reputation for capability and became harsh and fussy.
無復能名 means he no longer had a reputation for ability, not that a humane magistrate vanished; 苛碎 is harsh and fussy, and the office titles match 衛尉、河南尹、大司農.
The prefect had Pan Jing draft the proper notice; Luoyang adopted it as precedent.
He then had Jing compose a text and sent him to the capital, taking it as the permanent precedent.
遂遣京作文，使詣京師，以為永式 has Jing compose a text and go to the capital as a lasting model; the original invents Luoyang and a 'proper notice'.
His elder sister had married into the Sun clan and died early, leaving a grandson Mai; Guang carried him south in flight; though bandits pressed hard, he never abandoned the child.
His elder sister had married into the Sun clan and died early, leaving a son named Mai; Guang carried him south in flight; though bandits pressed hard, he never abandoned the child.
After 姊適孫氏, 有孫名邁 names the sister's son Sun Mai, the nephew Guang carried; reading 孫 as 'grandson' invents an extra generation.
Rated ‘brilliant’ second grade, he taught literature for Prince Wu, tutored the heir, and joined Prince Donghai Sima Yue's staff.

Rated ‘brilliant’ second grade, he became literary instructor to the Prince of Wu, then served in succession as Foreman Clerk of the Heir Apparent (xianma) and as adjutant to Sima Yue, Prince of Donghai.
吳王文學 is the office of literary instructor, 太子洗馬 is Foreman Clerk of the Heir Apparent rather than informal tutoring, and 曆 marks successive posts including 東海王越參軍.
Huan Yi and Yu Wei inspected the hungry, then impeached him for opening stores.
The court sent Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary Huan Yi, together with Yu, to comfort the starving and see whether affairs stood well, then impeached You for issuing grain without authorization.
臺遣散騎常侍桓彝、虞慰勞饑人 sends Huan Yi and a man surnamed Yu to comfort the hungry; 慰勞 is the verb 'to comfort', not a given name Wei.
In the second year of Taining, Mingdi plotted against Wang Dun by moving Deng You to Kuaiji.
In the second year of Taining, when Wang Dun rebelled, Emperor Ming secretly planned to raise troops and thereupon transferred You to Administrator of Kuaiji.
The Chinese sequences 王敦反, then 明帝密謀起兵, then 乃遷攸為會稽太守; the original wrongly treats the Kuaiji transfer as itself the plot against Wang Dun.
Wu Yin-zhi (courtesy Chumo) of Juancheng descended six generations from Wei attendant Wu Zhi.
Wu Yin-zhi (courtesy Chumo), a man of Juancheng in Puyang, was a sixth-generation descendant of Wei attendant Wu Zhi.
濮陽鄄城人 locates him in Juancheng of Puyang; omitting 濮陽 drops a stated native-place element.
He mourned his father so loudly strangers wept.
When he was a little over ten he suffered his father's death; whenever he wailed, passersby wept.
年十餘，丁父憂 dates the father's death to when Yin-zhi was a little over ten; the original drops that age.
Liu Yu demanded his release; months passed before he sailed home.
Liu Yu wrote Xun ordering Yin-zhi returned; only after a long interval did he come back.
劉裕與循書 is a letter ordering return, and 久方得反 is an unspecified long interval, not 'months' or a demand without a letter.
Yet Deng You tying his son abandoned kinship—if fate forced choice, why bind the boy to a tree?

Yet You abandoned his son to preserve his nephew, severing affection by righteousness—if strength truly failed, one might cut feeling and endure pain—why beforehand bind him with fetters and cut off one who would run to help!
棄子存侄，以義斷恩 and 預加徽纆，絕其奔走 name preserving the nephew and binding with fetters; the original invents a tree and omits the nephew.

Shiying exhausted fidelity to the house of Cao, forcing gates and breaking barriers; the Emperor Xuan unleashed thunderbolt wrath yet rewarded steadfast martyrdom—is it not that once mastery rested with him, he desired men whose integrity even critics must acknowledge!

Shiying exhausted fidelity to the house of Cao, forcing gates and breaking barriers; Emperor Xuan held back thunderbolt wrath and rewarded steadfast loyalty—is it not that once mastery rested with him, he desired men whose integrity even critics must acknowledge!
收雷霆之威 is holding back or withdrawing wrath, not unleashing it; 獎忠貞之烈 rewards ardent loyalty, not martyrdom.
